author: felipeblassioli@gmail.com
abstract: Triage-first skill for using Google Cloud Logging effectively against noisy output. Teaches the noise model (one request fans out across the Cloud Run stdout/stderr/requests streams, app loggers re-emit errors, entries repeat large header/context blobs, and the GCP `trace` joins streams while the app `traceId` does not) and a top-down triage funnel: locate by resource+time, pick one stream, floor severity, narrow to the symptom, and project only signal fields. Covers both the Logs Explorer query language and `gcloud logging read` (same filter language; operators and flags verified against the official docs). Secondary coverage of reducing noise at the source: emitter fixes (stop logging the Authorization Bearer token and full headers, collapse duplicate emits, drop empty context blobs), severity hygiene, exclusion filters on the _Default sink, and routing to dedicated buckets. Bundles scripts/triage-logs.sh, a jq-backed extractor that collapses an export to one row per trace and never prints the header/context blobs, so it is safe to run on exports containing secrets. Field paths use an example structured-log jsonPayload shape (adapt to your logger) but the technique is generic GCP.
